transcript.text: In this lecture, we will solve this problem which I have taken from gate 2000 electronics and communication engineering exam and according to the problem we are required to find the voltage VT and when you look at the network you will find VT is the voltage across this one Henry inductor and apart from this inductor we have two current sources in the network and this current source is providing the current equal to E power AT in this direction and this current source is providing the current equal to E power BT in this direction and we also have two resistors having the value one ohm each and we can find out voltage VT if we can find out the current through the inductor. So the first thing on which we will focus is the current through the inductor and we will calculate the current through the inductor using the nodal analysis and we know in nodal analysis we first find out the principal nodes and in this network this is one principal node and this is the another principal node. So in total we have two principal nodes and then we will choose the reference node and I have chosen the bottom node as the reference node and let's say this node is having the potential V1 and now we will write down the KCL equation at node 1 and to write down the KCL equation we will first mark the currents and we will mark the currents keeping in mind that V1 is the largest potential in the network and therefore all the three currents will leave the node 1. Let's say this current is current I1, this current is current I2 and this current is current I3 and according to KCL I1 plus I2 plus I3 will be equal to 0 and we can see that current I1 is equal to minus e power at because e power at is the current in this direction and I1 is the current in the opposite direction in the same branch therefore they will have the same magnitude but opposite directions and hence I1 will be equal to minus e power at therefore in place of I1 I will write minus e power at plus I2 then you can see that I3 will be equal to minus e power bt minus e power bt equal to 0 from here we can find out current I2, I2 is equal to e power at plus e power bt so now we have current I2 which is the current through our inductor and therefore now it is not difficult to calculate the voltage vt we know in case of an inductor the voltage is equal to the inductance multiplied to the time rate of change of current that is di2 by dt I2 is equal to this therefore vt will be equal to l and l is equal to 1 so 1 multiplied to d by dt e power at plus e power bt and we know when we differentiate when we differentiate e power at then we will have a multiplied to e power at similarly when we differentiate e power bt we will have b multiplied to e power bt therefore finally we are going to get the voltage vt equal to a multiplied to e power at plus b multiplied to e power bt and when you compare the result with the four options you will find option d is the correct option so this is all for the problem and now we will move on to our homework problem which I have taken from gate 1997 electronics and communication engineering paper and in this problem you are required to find the voltage v which is the voltage across this three ohm resistor the problem is not at all difficult so try to solve it and once you have your answer post it in comment section
